chunks: And Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about buying from the land of the Jews and Christians, so he said: 'There is no harm in it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) conquered the people of Khaybar and made a treaty with them to leave the land in their hands, so they would work it and cultivate it. Therefore, I see no harm if you buy something from it. And whoever people revive a piece of land and work it, they are more entitled to it, and it is theirs.'

key_terms.فَخَارَجَهُمْ: And made a treaty with them

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy land from Jews and Christians in Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to establish the juristic principle of *ibha'* (reviving dead land) as a basis for ownership transfer to non-Muslims, specifically citing the Prophet’s treaty with the Jews of Khaybar where they retained their land in exchange for tribute. This precedent supports the permissibility of purchasing agricultural land from *Ahl al-Kitab*, reinforcing the Shia view that cultivation rights supersede other claims, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic emphasis on stewardship and productive use of the earth.
